A [[Center (basketball)|center]], he was selected by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the [[2007 NBA draft]] and is the nephew of [[Steve Hawes]], a retired NBA player.[http://www.nba.com/draft2007/profiles/SpencerHawes.html NBA.com: 2007 NBA Draft Board-Spencer Hawes] ==High school career== Hawes played [[Center (basketball)|center]] at [[Seattle Preparatory School]], an elite college-[[University-preparatory school|prep school]] in [[Seattle|Seattle, Washington]]. The team won the state championship in the 2005–06 season and Hawes was named the tournament MVP. He might have entered the [[2006 NBA draft]] had the NBA not enacted a new rule requiring players to wait a year after their class graduates from high school. Following the 2005–06 season, Hawes was selected as an [[Associated Press]] [[All-American]], [[McDonald's All-American]], [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]], and [[USA Today]] All-American.usatoday.com [https://web.archive.org/web/20060428024818/https://www.usatoday.com/sports/preps/basketball/2006-04-17-boys-all-usa-team_x.htm All-USA basketball team] He was also named 2006 [[Gatorade]] Boys Basketball Washington Player of the Year and ''[[Seattle Times]]'' player of the year. Considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], Hawes was listed as the No. 2 center and the No. 6 player in the nation in 2006.yahoo.com [https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Spencer-Hawes-28437;_ylt=AhB.3hBL5kHEXvaJE8MKvstGPZB4 Spencer Hawes Recruiting Profile] He also was nicknamed “Baby Calf” by his high school teammates because of how awkwardly he would move outside the basketball court, attributed by his quick growth spurt from 6’4 his freshman year to 6’11 by his senior year. ==College career== Hawes attended and played at the University of Washington, where his uncle, [[Steve Hawes|Steve]], and his father, Jeff, both played basketball. Hawes led the Huskies in scoring with 14.9 points per game, ranked 10th in the Pac-10. Hawes also ranked second on the Huskies with 6.4 rebounds per game, ninth in the Pac-10. Spencer Hawes set a school record for freshmen with 461 points, despite missing one game due to a left ankle sprain. This record was later broken by [[Isaiah Thomas (basketball)|Isaiah Thomas]]. Hawes scored 20 or more points nine times, while posting three double-doubles. He was also named to the Pac-10 all-freshman team.[https://web.archive.org/web/20190104231138/https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2007/news/story?id=2908595 ESPN Hawes Only Plays One Year at Washington] ==Professional career== ===Sacramento Kings (2007–2010)=== Hawes was projected to go as high as fifth overall to the Celtics to as low as twelfth overall to the 76ers. He was drafted by the Sacramento Kings with the 10th overall pick in the [[2007 NBA draft]]. Hawes played sparingly in his rookie season of 2007/2008. Although appearing in 71 games, he started only 8 and averaged 13.1 minutes per game. He averaged a modest 4.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, and .6 blocks per game with a .459 field goal percentage. In his second season as a pro, opportunities opened up for Hawes when the starting center [[Brad Miller (basketball)|Brad Miller]] was traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]]. Hawes' numbers went up in every major statistical category, at 11.4 points, 7.1 rebounds, and 1.2 blocks per game with a .466 field goal percentage in 29.3 minutes per game. Hawes also started in 51 games, but missed the final game of the season due to an injury that occurred from a flagrant foul assessed to [[Kenyon Martin]] of the [[Denver Nuggets]].[https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news;_ylt=AhKyQDcMfZZHvKxINvC5Hu.TPaB4?slug=ap-kings-hawes&prov=ap&type=lgns Kings C Hawes done for season] The foul would result in controversy as Kings co-owner, Joe Maloof, would later state, "That (the hard foul) was thuggery, and you can quote me on that."[http://sacbee.com/kings/story/1780991.html Joe Maloof irate at Martin for way he fouled Hawes] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090418053226/http://www.sacbee.com/kings/story/1780991.html |date=2009-04-18 }} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2010–2014)=== On June 17, 2010, he was traded along with [[Andrés Nocioni]] to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] for center [[Samuel Dalembert]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/100617_trade.html |title=Sixers announce three-player trade with Kings |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2010-06-17 |access-date=2010-06-18}} Hawes ended the [[2010-11 NBA season]] having averaged 7.2 points per game. On March 16, 2013, Hawes recorded 18 points, 16 rebounds, 8 assists and 7 blocks in a win against the [[Indiana Pacers]].[http://www.nba.com/games/20130316/INDPHI/gameinfo.html Pacers at 76ers, March 16, 2013] On November 22, 2013, Hawes recorded 25 points, 12 rebounds, and 2 assists in a 115–107 OT victory over the Milwaukee Bucks. Hawes hit a clutch three pointer with 3.9 seconds left on the clock to send the game to overtime.[http://www.nba.com/games/20131122/MILPHI/gameinfo.html Notebook: Sixers 115, Bucks 107 (OT)] In the 2013–14 season, Hawes was ranked 12th for three point field goal percentage in 2013–14.[https://www.espn.com/nba/stats/player NBA Player 3-Point Shooting Statistics – 2013–14] ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2014)=== On February 20, 2014, Hawes was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in exchange for [[Earl Clark]], [[Henry Sims]] and two future second-round picks.[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/cavs-acquire-hawes-140220 Cavs Acquire Spencer Hawes from 76ers] ===Los Angeles Clippers (2014–2015)=== On July 9, 2014, Hawes signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].[http://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-sign-farmar-and-hawes CLIPPERS SIGN FARMAR AND HAWES] He had a 15-game starting stretch during February and March while teammate [[Blake Griffin]] recovered from a [[staph infection]]. During this stretch, he tied his season-high of 17 points in a loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder on February 8.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/hawessp01/gamelog/2015/ Spencer Hawes 2014–15 Game Log] ===Charlotte Hornets (2015–2017)=== On June 15, 2015, Hawes was traded, along with [[Matt Barnes]], to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in exchange for [[Lance Stephenson]].{{cite web|title=Hornets Acquire Spencer Hawes and Matt Barnes from the Los Angeles Clippers in Exchange for Lance Stephenson|date=June 15, 2015|work=NBA.com|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-acquire-spencer-hawes-and-matt-barnes-los-angeles-clippers-exchange-lance-stephenson|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150616122948/http://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-acquire-spencer-hawes-and-matt-barnes-los-angeles-clippers-exchange-lance-stephenson|archive-date=June 16, 2015|url-status=live}} During the Hornets' 2016 first-round playoff series against the Miami Heat, Hawes sustained a sprained medial collateral ligament in his right knee.[http://www.nba.com/2016/news/04/28/spencer-hawes-out-for-rest-of-series-vs-heat.ap/ Hornets' Hawes out for remainder of series vs Heat] ===Milwaukee Bucks (2017)=== On February 2, 2017, Hawes was traded, along with [[Roy Hibbert]], to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in exchange for [[Miles Plumlee]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-acquire-spencer-hawes-and-roy-hibbert-charlotte|title=Bucks Acquire Spencer Hawes and Roy Hibbert from Charlotte|work=NBA.com|date=February 2, 2017|access-date=February 2, 2017}} Hawes didn't see a single minute of action in the first 11 games after he was acquired by the Bucks.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900315|title=Middleton's season-high 24 points lead Bucks past Raptors|work=ESPN.com|date=March 4, 2017|access-date=March 5, 2017}} He made his debut on March 3 with a late three-minute stint against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. The following day, he turned in a game-changing performance, scoring 14 second-quarter points, including back-to-back three-pointers and an acrobatic layup while drawing a foul, to spark the Bucks to a 101–94 win over the [[Toronto Raptors]]. He finished the game with 16 points, two shy of his season high, and eight rebounds in 17 minutes. On September 1, 2017, he was waived by the Bucks.{{cite web|title=Bucks request waivers on Spencer Hawes|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-request-waivers-spencer-hawes|website=NBA.com|date=September 1, 2017|access-date=September 1, 2017}} ===South Bay Lakers (2019)=== On March 2, 2019, Hawes signed with the [[South Bay Lakers]].{{cite web|last1=Camarena|first1=Noah|title=South Bay Lakers acquire Spencer Hawes|url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-claim-spencer-hawes/|website=NBA G League|access-date=March 10, 2019|date=March 2, 2019|archive-date=February 26, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210226042848/https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-claim-spencer-hawes/|url-status=dead}} ==National team career== Hawes debuted for USA Basketball in April 2006 as a member of the 2006 USA Junior National Select Team that defeated the World Select Team 109–91 at the Nike Hoop Summit in Memphis, Tenn. In the summer of 2006, Hawes led all scorers with 24 points and added 10 rebounds, contributing to a United States men's team victory over Argentina in the gold medal game of the FIBA Americas under-18 Championship by a score of 104–82.[http://www.nba.com/draft2007/profiles/SpencerHawes.html NBA.com profile Spencer Hawes] Overall, Hawes averaged 12.0 points and 7.5 rebounds during the tournament.
